subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a full module for a stone gargoyle crouched on a ledge, facing forward, with a grey-and-moss stone palette, and sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hip joint.

Still defining the spine chain...

Neck gets two spans parented to the spine's last joint, with the spine endpoint coinciding with the neck start so they connect seamlessly, using a tapered radius sweep. For the head, I'm placing the joint at the neck's end point with a forward-facing direction, using local coordinate words like "left," "up," and "forward" to position symmetric features without worrying about raw axis signs, then building the skull as a box attached to the head bone.

For the skull and face, I'm sizing a slightly forward-and-up offset box for the cranium, adding a protruding brow ridge above where the eyes will go, and a smaller snout box projecting forward. I'm giving the jaw its own joint just below and in front of the head joint so the upper snout stays fixed while the lower jaw can be posed open at a slight angle after the geometry is built, then adding small downward-pointing cone teeth on the upper jaw.

Now I'm placing glowing amber eye spheres with dark recessed eye sockets behind them using the glow kit, and sketching out curved horn sweeps as bezier curves anchored to head-local points with tapering point-capped geometry.

Next I'm defining pointed bat-like ear shapes as simple non-self-intersecting polygon outlines extruded with thickness, positioned at the sides of the head, then moving on to sketch a browridge box shape.

Then I'm adding small nostril boxes for the nose and a wedge shape for a goatee, and placing a row of spikes along the spine using a sweep-based body so each spike points outward along the dorsal normal rather than tangent to the chain.

For the arms, I'm working out a crouched gargoyle pose with front legs planted forward on the ledge: shoulders mounted high and out, hands reaching down to the ledge surface, checking the reach distance stays within limb length limits, and bending the elbow backward and outward for the hunched stance.

Still defining the arm chain and hand geometry...

Still placing hand and foot positions, then working out the hind leg haunch geometry with hip, knee, and foot joints positioned for a crouched stance on the ledge.

Now I'm sketching the folded bat-like wings rising behind the back, starting from the shoulder joints.

Still defining finger chains...

For the fingers I'll use rod sweeps with thin thickness, and connect membranes between consecutive finger edges plus one to the body edge, skipping extra leading-edge membranes for simplicity—stone-carved gargoyle wings with a slightly lighter, thicker ribbed membrane to read as carved rock. Now I'm starting the tail as a curving catmull chain sweeping back and up from the hips.

I'm giving the tail a tapering radius with a small arrowhead spike at the tip oriented along the tangent, then checking that it clears the ledge surface it drapes over, and sizing the ledge geometry to support it.

Now I'm detailing the ledge itself with cornice moulding and carved surface decoration — adding trefoil rings and a blind arcade of pointed-arch shapes across the front face.

I'm also adding surface wear and weathering touches: moss patches flattened onto the ledge top and gargoyle shoulders, lichen, and small chips, settling on a stone color palette with warm greys and a mossy green accent.

For the stone body material, I'm using the mottle paint combined with countershade so the surface reads darker toward the bottom, mimicking rain staining and weathering, sticking to proven paint functions rather than inventing new ones. I'm also considering a faceted, slightly stylized look for the sweeps by adjusting the polygon sides.

For faceted shading, I'll set smooth to false with eight sides for a chunky, carved-stone look, and I'm using low-detail icosahedrons with flat shading for the shoulders, haunches, and chest to give rough chunky plate forms. I'm also thinking about spine ridge spikes along the back and tail, plus a small gothic chest emblem using a thin torus ring facing forward as a decorative detail.

I'm figuring out how to place that torus accurately: using nearest-surface lookup from a ray point to snap it onto the chest front, then rotating the torus geometry so its ring lies flat against the body surface. I'm estimating the chest's actual coordinates around y 0.6-0.7 to make sure the ring lands correctly, then planning additional rib band loops around the torso for extra ornamentation.

I'm skipping the belt/loincloth and instead adding thin dark boxes as stone cracks and chips for texture. Now I'm setting up mirrored left/right helper functions and a head joint with local direction helpers, then starting to define the skull as a flat-shaded box with slightly beveled proportions positioned relative to the head origin.

Still working out the brow pieces, splitting them into two angled boxes per side that rotate around the z-axis to create a sloped, angry expression — tilting the outer edges upward for a fierce look.

Now I'm placing the eye sockets as dark spheres with glowing amber eyes nested inside, and considering adding a small dark slit pupil for extra detail.

Next I'm building the snout as a box for the upper jaw, adding a nose bridge wedge and dark nostril boxes positioned at the front, then placing flipped cone shapes for the upper fangs angled downward below the snout.

Now I'm setting up the jaw joint hierarchy, creating a lower jaw box bone and positioning upward-facing cone fangs beneath it, adjusting the y-coordinates so the lower jaw and fangs tuck slightly inside the snout for a closed-mouth rest pose while leaving room for the jaw to open in animation.

I'm adding a downward chin spike as a goatee-like cone attached to the jaw bone, then considering spiky frill fins along the back of the head using a jagged outline shape.

Still defining frill geometry...

Now I'm sketching the horns as curved bezier shapes swept back from the head, using control points positioned via the head's coordinate helper.

For ears I'm weighing placement options but deciding to skip them since they'd collide with the frill, keeping just the frill and horns for simplicity. I'll also add a flattened green moss patch on top of the head for extra detail.

Now I'm sketching the rest of the body: back spikes, a haunch using an icosahedron for the pelvis, shoulder pads attached to the arm bone, and the wing root parented to the spine joint. The gargoyle will sit directly on the ledge without extra plinth geometry, and I'm starting to define helper functions for creating boxes and icosahedron shapes before writing the full build code.

I'm defining the stone coloring using a countershaded mottle pattern so the top faces look weathered and the underside darker, plus a mossy tint for upward-facing surfaces, while sketching the ledge geometry with a base slab and upper cornice sized to fit the arches.

Still working out plinth and lip dimensions...

Repeating the arches across the ledge at even spacing, and thinking about whether side ledges or corbel details are needed—deciding to skip those for simplicity. For rigging, I'm figuring out that the ledge mesh should attach to the hips joint so it moves correctly with the rest of the body.

Writing builder code...

Settling hips at 0.42 with spine chain curving up to 0.76 for the belly bulge. Checking hind limb geometry—hip to ankle distance works out with knee bending forward and up into a natural crouch haunch position.

Now placing the hind foot with toe cones angled forward, and working out the arm geometry: shoulder to hand reach checks out at roughly 0.47, with elbow bending outward and back for a natural pose.

I'm naming all the chain joints consistently (shoulder/elbow/wrist for arms, hip/knee/ankle for legs) and parenting the hip chain to the hips. For the wings I'm setting up a root-elbow-wrist chain with upward-swept coordinates to give the wing a natural outstretched shape.

Now I'm defining the wing's finger bones as rods extending from the wrist to give it a folded, resting silhouette behind the body, along with the body's edge polyline.

I'm also working out which membrane quads connect adjacent finger/arm edges, checking that the start and end points pair up sensibly even where the wing arm and body edge diverge in position.

I'll set membrane thickness to about 2% of mean width and figure out the wrist bone joint index for attaching the wing. The skin color for the membrane gets a slightly different shade, with claws at the wrist and stone texture on the fingers, then I move on to defining the tail starting from the hips.

Mapping the tail curve down toward the ground and checking radius tapering so it doesn't clip, I name the segments tail1 through tail4 and add a spike tip near the end. Then I work out how the back ledge, plinth, and front lip dimensions need to shift to accommodate where the tail terminates, adjusting the arch placement accordingly.

Now I'm adding tail spikes along the sweep, dorsal spikes along the body, and detailing a chest emblem with a ring and inner petal pattern. I plan moss patches as flattened spheres on the ledge and gargoyle's back, and consider skipping rune stripes on the forearms in favor of simple knuckle spheres.

I'm setting up a helper function for faceted parts with flat shading enabled by default, then placing eye pupils, a lower jaw box, and deciding to skip horn rings and head tilt for simplicity before finalizing the full build and export.

Now I'm adding the frill as an extruded outline attached to the head bone, and defining brow rotations using Euler angles. I'm also adding wing claw spikes with normalized direction vectors pointing up and outward from the wrist joint.
